How the schedule is calculated

A deterministic heuristic tries several activity orderings, packs compatible co-workers into shared possessions and compares the published penalty scores. Every activity receives at most one access per week. Extended nights (ECLO) deliver 1.5 work units; standard nights deliver 1.

Lower scores are better. A scores priority-weighted delay; B scores 7 × extra location-week access slots + 5 × ECLO nights; C combines both. This is a heuristic, not a guarantee of the globally best schedule.

Validation scope and planning assumptions

Checks cover workload, start weeks, predecessor order, possession mixes, route spans, buffers, Live closures, weekly limits, workfronts, capacity and ECLO windows. The organiser’s reference validator was not supplied. A passed check here is not official validation or approval for railway operations.

Possession group labels are consistent dispatch slots across a route; contractor access-night indices are separate local accounting values. Buffer conflicts are checked within each dispatch slot. Co-sharing is limited to overlapping non-Live spans with legal mixes. Supply repeats weekly, including beyond the nominal horizon. All results must be checked against the organiser’s validator before submission.
